name: Spine — Mirage Console
thesis: Mirage Console is a workspace-scoped developer debug console built as a single dominant organism: a chronological ACTION STREAM down the left, a reconstructed STATE TREE down the right, and a TRANSPORT (play/pause/step/jump/skip) wired to a time-travel cursor that sweeps both. This is Redux DevTools, literally — except the "store" is a live mirage workspace and the actions are real data-plane I/O, not the model's self-reported tool args. You open a workspace, see every action that ever flowed through it (AG-UI run/step/reasoning/tool-call events, VfsOps from the OpRecord ground-truth leaf, relay command/op/mock events), drop the cursor on any action, and watch the right pane render the exact workspace state at that instant with the single mutation this action caused highlighted. The trace waterfall is NOT a separate page — it is a *grouping lens* that collapses the same flat action list by run/step/tool-call. Data Sources is a *docked panel*, not a destination, because mirage IS the data plane: the same OpRecords that are actions are also the access log for every mounted backend, so "scrub the workspace's life and watch state mutate" and "click a file, see which actions touched it" are two views of one event log. Governance is demoted to quiet per-write decorations (a small effect-class dot, a reversibility tooltip) — there is no pending-effects counter in the chrome, no LIVE red banner, no promote modal as a front door. We commit hardest to one feel: an engineer scrubbing a deterministic, exportable, diff-highlighted timeline of everything their agent did to real data, all day, from the keyboard.
organizingMetaphor: Redux DevTools, taken literally and without apology: a single persistent two-pane shell — Action List (left) + State Inspector (right) — with a time-travel transport bar pinned across the bottom. There is no "home page" and no top-level page switcher in the usual sense; the Event Log IS the home and IS the structure. Everything else (the trace waterfall, data-source exploration, the run-level reasoning view) is expressed as a *lens* or *dock* over that same spine and same cursor, exactly as Redux DevTools offers Log / Chart / Diff / State tabs over one action list. The mental model the dev carries: "this workspace is a store; these are its dispatched actions; I can rewind it."
informationArchitecture:
TOP-LEVEL CONTAINER = workspace. A slim 44px global header holds only: (1) a workspace switcher combobox (left), (2) the active branch chip + a tiny mode glyph (TEST/LIVE shown as a 1-char monospace tag, never red chrome), (3) a connection dot + persisted/in-memory state pill, and (4) a global keyboard-driven command palette (Cmd-K). No sub-nav tabs row like the current ConsoleLayout SUB_NAV — that page-switcher mental model is deleted.

Below the header is THE SPINE, a fixed three-region grid that never unmounts:
- LEFT RAIL (380px, resizable): the unified ACTION LIST — one virtualized, reverse-chronological-or-chronological log of every action in the workspace, with a filter/type-chip bar pinned at its top and a transport footer at its bottom.
- CENTER+RIGHT (fluid): the STATE INSPECTOR for the action under the cursor. A lens selector sits at the very top of this region (Diff · State Tree · Action · Trace · Data) — these are TABS over the SAME selected action and SAME cursor, not separate routes.
- TRANSPORT BAR (bottom, 36px, full width): the time-travel scrubber — a horizontal mini-map of the action stream with the cursor, plus play/pause/step-back/step-fwd/jump-to-end, a speed control, and "actions N of M | cursor at #K".
- DATA DOCK (right edge, 0–420px, collapsible): the Data Sources explorer (mount tree + file browser). Collapsed by default to a 36px vertical strip of mount color-dots; expands as a docked panel, NOT a full page. Selecting a file here cross-links into the action list (reverse-link).

HOW A DEV MOVES:
- All traces ↔ single trace: there is no navigation — toggle the action list's GROUPING control between 'Flat' (every action) and 'By run/step' (the waterfall lens). 'By run/step' collapses the same rows into a Run › Step › ToolCall › VfsOp tree in-place in the left rail; the right inspector's Trace lens shows the selected node's waterfall. Selecting any leaf still moves the one global cursor.
- Single trace ↔ event log / time-travel: they are the same thing. Time-travel is not a mode you enter; the cursor always exists. Clicking any action = jump-to that action. The transport just animates the cursor.
- → Data sources: open the Data Dock (Cmd-\\ or click the strip). It is anchored to the right so the action list and inspector stay visible — you browse data WHILE watching the timeline.
- Data source → traces: clicking a path in the Data Dock filters the action list to "actions that touched this path" and badges the matching rows; clicking one of those rows moves the cursor. This is the bidirectional bridge, kept on-screen simultaneously rather than as a separate page.

URL/permalink scheme makes every position addressable: /w/:workspaceId?cursor=:seqOrIdx&lens=diff&group=step&path=/s3/foo — so any action+lens+data-selection is a shareable deep link (reuses the existing per-node permalink idea from the prior design).
reduxMapping:
ACTION LIST ← the merged event stream, rendered as Redux-style rows: [index] [type chip] [terse payload summary] [Δ badge]. Two honest indices coexist and are shown explicitly: relay firehose events carry the process-global `seq` (from _persist_and_broadcast/_next_stream_seq, stable across restart); AG-UI run events carry only a per-session `agui_events.seq` + ms timestamp. Because no single monotonic key spans both (the two-counter problem), the merged ordering is by timestamp and is rendered with a subtle 'inferred order' hairline marker wherever same-ms events collide; the row's left gutter shows seq for firehose rows and §seq for agui rows so the dev never thinks they're one counter. Action 'type' = event `.type` (RUN_STARTED, STEP_STARTED, TOOL_CALL_START/ARGS/RESULT/END, THINKING_*, TEXT_MESSAGE_*, CUSTOM(vfs_op), and relay command/op/mock_request/agent_status). The VfsOp rows are special-cased as the ground-truth leaf and carry the gap-free op `idx` (== position in ws.ops.records) — this is the CLEAN cursor for state reconstruction.

STATE TREE ← reconstructed workspace state at the cursor, folded from trajectory[0..idx] (and the AG-UI reducer for the run sub-tree). The right 'State Tree' lens shows a collapsible JSON-ish tree with four top-level nodes, each backed by real endpoints: (1) overlay — per-mount write-set from _console_overlay, change key idx:op:path; (2) mounts — prefix/resource/mode/effect_class from _console_mounts_detail; (3) reads-so-far — the set of read ops up to idx from _console_trajectory; (4) run — runs/steps/toolCalls/messages from replayAguiEvents folded to the cursor's timestamp. A fifth node 'state (snapshot)' is rendered as a reserved, dimmed 'not yet emitted' stub because STATE_SNAPSHOT/STATE_DELTA are dead enum names (never emitted/reduced/stored) — we show the slot to be honest about the Redux ideal without faking it.

ACTION DIFF ← diff(stateAt(idx-1), stateAt(idx)), and this is where mirage shines: for a VfsOp action the diff is EXACT and trivial — action idx is exactly OpRecord[idx], so the diff is precisely that one op (path, op kind, +bytes, source, effect-class), rendered green/amber/red like a git hunk. For run-level actions we diff successive reducer snapshots (a new message delta, a newly-started step, a tool result arriving). The existing OverlayDiff component is the seed of the per-write hunk renderer.

JUMP-TO ← clicking an action sets cursor=idx and re-folds entries[0..idx] (pure client-side, deterministic — replayAguiEvents already proves fold-from-empty). SKIP-ACTION ← right-click an action › 'Skip' re-folds entries[0..idx] minus the skipped idx, and the row renders struck-through with a 'skipped' tag; this is honest for the overlay/reads-so-far/run sub-tree (recomputable) and is DISABLED with a tooltip for backing-dependent state. FUTURE-DIMMING ← every row with index > cursor renders at 45% opacity with a thin 'not yet executed' left border; the transport mini-map dims the future segment. IMPORT/EXPORT ← Export already exists (TrajectoryPage exportJson dumps entries); we generalize it to export the full merged action log + the per-session agui_events trace as one .mirage-session.json. Import re-hydrates the action list and run sub-tree via replayAguiEvents for offline scrubbing; it is labeled 'replay (state reconstruction from pinned backing deferred)' because the backing tar is pinned once at stand-up, so imported sessions scrub the run/overlay/reads layers but cannot byte-reconstruct written-mount full-FS.

HONESTY OVERLAYS ON THE REDUX MODEL: (a) cache hits emit no OpRecord, so the action list has real gaps vs true I/O — a derived 'served from cache' chip appears on the read action it accelerated, never as a phantom action. (b) the 20-op-per-command cap on relay `op` events means the firehose can under-count vs the uncapped AG-UI CUSTOM path; the action list prefers the agui/trajectory source for VfsOps and flags any firehose-only discrepancy. (c) op→step/run attribution is INFERRED (timestamp-window bucketing, correlateEvents.ts) until tool_call_id is stamped at emission — every grouped row carries a tiny 'inferred' dot in the By-step lens.
dataSourceExploration:
The Data Dock is a docked right-edge panel (not a page) that treats mirage's unified VFS for what it is: a mount tree + per-path file browser, because every backend (S3, Slack, Postgres, Datadog) is mounted behind one filesystem and — in the shipped northhill_corp demo — is literally a Fake*Resource(DiskResource), i.e. JSON/JSONL files on disk dressed as exotic sources. So we do NOT build per-backend native widgets; we build ONE tree+preview that is honest about that.

TOP LEVEL = mount list from _console_mounts_detail over Workspace.mounts(): each row shows prefix (/s3, /database, /datadog, /slack, ram '/'), resource type name, mode (read/write/exec), and a quiet derived effect-class dot (scratch/durable-internal/system-of-record/external-effect) with a reversibility tooltip — this is the most solid per-source metadata we have. Expanding a mount calls vfsList (GET /api/sessions/{id}/vfs → shell `ls -la` → _parse_ls_output) to lazy-load a directory tree of {name,type,size} ONLY. Selecting a file calls vfsFile (→ `cat`) and previews decoded text, JSON pretty-printed client-side. Every preview header carries a mandatory honesty strip: 'preview only · text decode · no binary/truncation detection' and, when size is large, a 'truncated' marker — because the ls/cat path drops modified-time/fingerprint/revision/mode/consistency and has no binary handling. A 'Tables' affordance: when a directory matches the disk-fake table layout (tables/<t>/schema.json+data.jsonl+stats.json) we offer a 'view as table/schema' toggle that renders schema.json columns and the first rows of data.jsonl in a grid — explicitly labeled 'read from files · no live query'. The query.json / catalog-proxy (Iceberg/Snowflake/MCP) live-query path is shown as a single greyed 'Query' affordance with a 'not yet implemented' tag (all NotImplementedError stubs; no Snowflake/Postgres adapter exists) — present as the aspiration, never callable. Per-path fingerprint/revision/consistency get a reserved metadata row that reads 'not surfaced (S3-only via ETag; demo backends are disk-backed)' so we never fake drift UI on disk doubles.

THE BIDIRECTIONAL BRIDGE (the moat) is the dock's whole reason to exist: selecting any path flips the action list into 'touched by' mode — it filters to every action whose VfsOp path startswith the selection (derived from ws.ops.records via _console_trajectory keyed by mount_prefix+path), showing each read/write with bytes/duration/source/effect-class and its op idx. A header reads 'N actions touched /s3/reports/q3.csv — 3 reads, 1 write'. Clicking one of those actions moves the global cursor, so the State Inspector jumps to the moment that byte was read/written and the Diff lens highlights exactly that op. Conversely, the inverse link is always live: when the cursor sits on a VfsOp action, the Data Dock auto-reveals and highlights that path in the tree (scroll-into-view + ring), so 'who touched this byte' and 'what did this action touch' are the same gesture from two directions. HONESTY: the path→op join is exact (records carry mount_prefix+path); the path→step/run attribution is INFERRED by event ordering (ops between two TOOL_CALL_STARTs belong to that exec) and every bridged row carries the 'inferred' dot until tool_call_id is stamped at emission. mock_request/mcp_tool_call rows will be near-empty unless an external eval agent feeds POST /ingest, and the dock says so rather than showing a blank Datadog/Slack pane as if broken.

leveragesMirageData: Deeply, and only in ways the real plumbing supports. The spine's action rows for VfsOps come from the OpRecord ground-truth leaf (observe/record.py: op·path·source·bytes·duration_ms·mount_prefix·fingerprint·revision·is_cache) surfaced via _console_trajectory, which also gives the gap-free op `idx` used as the reconstruction cursor. State-at-cursor folds real endpoints: _console_overlay (per-mount write-set, change key idx:op:path — the OverlayDiff seed), _console_mounts_detail (prefix/resource/mode/effect_class via _effect_class_for_mount), and reads-so-far from the same trajectory; the run sub-tree is rebuilt by replayAguiEvents over getSessionTrace's agui_events (proven deterministic fold-from-empty). The action diff for a write is literally the OpRecord at idx. The Data Dock is the real VFS browse path (vfsList/vfsFile → shell ls/cat → _parse_ls_output) plus _console_mounts_detail, and the reverse-link is ws.ops.records filtered by mount_prefix+path (exact). The merged firehose uses the genuine relay StreamEvent feed (_persist_and_broadcast, global seq, /events SSE, useEventStream) unioned with per-session agui_events. Effect-class/reversibility decorations come straight from the console's effect classifier. Export generalizes the real TrajectoryPage exportJson. Crucially, the design is honest where the data is thin: cache 'hits' are derived from is_cache/absence-of-network-op (never faked as actions), backing/full-FS time travel is rendered as 'pinned at stand-up' (one snapshot tar, not per-tick), STATE_SNAPSHOT/STATE_DELTA appear as a reserved dimmed node (dead enum names), fingerprint/revision/consistency show 'not surfaced' on disk-backed demo sources, query.json/catalog-proxy is a greyed 'not implemented' chip, and op→step/run attribution wears an 'inferred' dot until tool_call_id is stamped (the named Phase-0 fix). The two-counter reality (relay seq vs per-session agui seq, timestamp-merged) is shown in the row gutter and an 'inferred order' hairline rather than pretending one global index exists.
risks: The two-counter merge is the structural soft spot: with no single monotonic key spanning relay seq and per-session agui seq, same-ms actions have undefined order, so the 'scrub everything in one stream' promise is timestamp-approximate. Mitigation: show seq/§seq in the gutter and an 'inferred order' marker; push the Phase-0 fix (route AG-UI through _persist_and_broadcast, stamp run/step/tool_call_id) to make it exact — but until then the spine's headline feel rests on an inferred ordering.

Time-travel sells 'watch state mutate', but only overlay/reads/run/pending-effects are truly reconstructable; written-mount full-FS backing is pinned once at stand-up. A dev may expect byte-exact rewind of file *contents* and be disappointed. Mitigation: the State Tree backing node and import banner both label this clearly, and Diff focuses on the exact, real op-level mutation rather than full-FS snapshots — but the gap must be communicated relentlessly or it reads as a bug.

On the shipped northhill_corp demo, every 'exotic' source (Postgres/Datadog/S3/Slack) is a Fake*Resource(DiskResource), so the Data Dock shows disk dirs dressed as backends, with no fingerprint/revision, no live query, and mock_request/mcp_tool_call usually empty (only POST /ingest feeds them). The dock could look underwhelming or 'broken'. Mitigation: explicit 'disk-backed · no live query · preview only' labeling and a 'view as table/schema' affordance to add value honestly; never render an empty native pane as if a real backend failed.

Scale: a console watching ALL workspace actions cannot ride the 2000/5000-event RAM rings or in-memory console caches. Without arcadia_store-backed pagination/virtualization (and read methods for vfs_ops/runs/steps which are currently WRITE-ONLY), the action list will truncate or go empty after restart. Mitigation: virtualize the list, paginate via /events?after=N and stored traces, and surface a 'persisted vs in-memory' pill — but this is real backend work, not just UI.

Committing this hard to the Redux spine demotes governance to near-invisible decorations; if a stakeholder still expects the ops/promote workflow to be reachable, the single quiet effect-class dot + tooltip may feel like a regression. Mitigation: keep promote reachable from the command palette and the per-write decoration, but accept that this paradigm deliberately is not a governance product.

ls/cat preview is text-only with no binary/truncation detection, so binary or huge files in the dock will mangle. Mitigation: mandatory 'preview only' strip, size-based truncation marker, and a future move to a structured FS read — but in the current build the fidelity ceiling is low and must be labeled, not hidden.

Skip/jump determinism holds for the run/overlay/reads fold, but skipping a read that fed a later write cannot retro-actively change the written bytes (backing is pinned); 'skip' is therefore a state-reconstruction tool, not a true re-execution. Mitigation: scope the Skip affordance to reconstructable layers and label it, reserving real re-drive for the deferred Replay-against-pin feature.

name: Mirage Workbench
thesis: A workspace-scoped developer debug console built like Chrome DevTools docked over a running app: the workspace IS the "page", and a single screen holds five draggable, simultaneously-visible panels — a Trace waterfall, a unified Event Log (the action stream), a Data Sources tree, a State inspector, and a Console/output dock — wired into one cross-filter bus. The defining move is that a single global cursor (a position in the action stream) drives every panel at once: click action N and the waterfall highlights the owning step, the data tree marks the paths touched at/through N, and the State inspector renders the workspace reconstructed AT N with a diff of exactly what that action changed. Because mirage observes the real data plane (path/bytes/source/cache/fingerprint at observe.context.record), the Workbench is the only debugger that can dock a data-plane span layer beneath every tool call AND be a live explorer of the connected sources themselves — and bridge them bidirectionally ("who touched this byte?"). Governance is demoted to a quiet per-write decoration; this is a tool an engineer lives in all day, not an ops inbox. Every panel is grounded in callable endpoints; reconstruction is honest (op-by-op overlay/reads/effects are exact, written-mount backing is labeled "pinned at stand-up"), and reserved panels (lineage/policy/STATE_SNAPSHOT) render as explicit "not yet emitted" rails rather than fabricated data.
organizingMetaphor: Chrome DevTools / VS Code docked over the workspace: the workspace is the inspected "page", and the screen is a persistent, user-arrangeable dock of panels (waterfall, event log, data tree, state inspector, console) tied together by one selection cursor and a command palette — you debug a workspace the way you debug a running web app, with the Redux DevTools time-travel cursor as the spine running across all panels.
informationArchitecture: TOP-LEVEL = WORKSPACE, always. A slim 40px top App Bar holds: (1) a workspace switcher dropdown (consoleStore.workspaces / setActiveWorkspace, persisted to localStorage) showing name · branch · mode; (2) a global Cursor Scrubber pill ("@ action 142 / 318 · live") that is the single time-travel cursor shared by every panel; (3) a command-palette trigger (Cmd-K); (4) a Layout menu (preset dock arrangements + reset); (5) a quiet connection dot (useEventStream connected) and a derived "pending N" micro-chip (no red chrome, no modal — demoted governance). Below it is ONE workbench surface — not routed pages. The five panels live in a react-resizable dock with draggable dividers and tabbed panel-groups (DevTools "panes"). Default layout: LEFT rail = Data Sources tree (260px, collapsible); CENTER-TOP = Trace waterfall; CENTER-BOTTOM = Event Log (the action stream, the tallest panel); RIGHT = State inspector (340px); BOTTOM dock = Console/output (collapsible drawer, like DevTools console). Any panel can be dragged to another dock zone, maximized (double-click header → solo), or stacked as tabs. NAVIGATION BETWEEN VIEWS is not page-switching — it is moving the cursor and the selection: (a) ALL-TRACES is the Event Log filtered to RUN_* + the Run rail at the top of the waterfall (each run = a collapsible lane); (b) A SINGLE TRACE = click a run lane → waterfall scopes to that run, Event Log filters to events whose run window contains them; (c) EVENT LOG / TIME-TRAVEL = the bottom-center panel itself, with the cursor; scrubbing it drives everything; (d) DATA SOURCES = the left tree, which both stands alone (browse) and reacts to the cursor (touched-path highlighting). A breadcrumb strip under the App Bar shows scope: Workspace ▸ Run ▸ Step ▸ ToolCall ▸ VfsOp, each segment a click-target that narrows the cross-filter. Deep-linkable: workspace id + cursor index + selected panel are encoded in the URL (?ws=…&cursor=142&sel=tc-… ) so any state is a permalink. Persistence/scale: panels read from arcadia_store-backed paginated endpoints with virtualization, never the 2000-event RAM ring directly; a "not persisted" badge appears if _setup_persistence degraded to memory.
reduxMapping: ACTION LIST ← the Event Log panel = the merged stream. Two real sources, honestly merged: the relay firehose (useEventStream('/events'), stable global `seq`, types command/op/agent_status/agent_thinking/mock_request/mcp_tool_call/console_*) UNION the per-session AG-UI events (getSessionTrace → RUN/STEP/THINKING/TEXT/TOOL_CALL/CUSTOM(vfs_op), per-session seq). Because AG-UI events carry NO global seq, the merge key is timestamp; same-ms ordering is undefined and the UI flags it with a faint "≈" tie-marker and a tooltip "ordered by timestamp; exact interleave pending Phase-0 seq plumbing." Each row's "action.type" = event .type; payload = the event dict (expand to a JSON tree). A PARALLEL, gap-free index runs alongside: the op-indexed Trajectory (getTrajectory → entries[].idx == position in ws.ops.records). The cursor stores BOTH (a stream position and the nearest trajectory idx) and prefers the trajectory idx for state reconstruction because it is dense and deterministic. STATE TREE INSPECTOR ← the State panel = workspace reconstructed at cursor by folding trajectory[0..idx]: (a) effective VFS overlay (getOverlay mounts[].changes, change key idx:op:path) = the write set so far; (b) mounts (getConsoleWorkspace.mounts: prefix/resource/mode/effect_class); (c) reads-so-far set (read ops ≤ idx); (d) pending effects (getEffects writes not in promoted_keys); (e) the run/step/tool sub-tree from aguiEventReducer (replayAguiEvents up to the cursor timestamp). PER-ACTION DIFF ← for a data-plane action the diff is exact and trivial: action N == OpRecord[idx], so the diff IS that single op (path, +bytes, op kind, source) rendered the way OverlayDiff renders one change, with the touched path flashed in the data tree; for a run-level action, diff successive reducer snapshots (new reasoning delta / new tool call / step boundary). JUMP-TO ← set cursor = clicked action's idx, re-fold [0..idx] (pure client-side over the trajectory array, the same deterministic fold replayAguiEvents already proves). SKIP-ACTION ← re-fold [0..idx] minus the skipped idx; rendered as a "what-if overlay" with a banner "hypothetical: action 88 skipped" and a one-click revert (we never claim the real run changed). FUTURE-DIMMING ← every Event Log row and every waterfall node with index > cursor renders at 40% opacity with a hairline "future" rule; the data tree dims paths only touched in the future. IMPORT/EXPORT ← Export already exists (TrajectoryPage exportJson dumps {workspace, entries}); the Workbench promotes it to "Export session bundle" = trajectory entries + agui_events trace (getSessionTrace) + workspace mounts/snapshot manifest, and adds IMPORT (load a bundle → replayAguiEvents + render the trajectory read-only with the cursor enabled) so a teammate can replay a saved debugging session offline. HONEST LIMITS surfaced inline: full byte-exact filesystem of WRITTEN mounts before N is NOT reconstructable (backing pinned once at stand-up) — the State panel's "Backing" tab is labeled "pinned at stand-up; pre-overlay reconstruction is a Replay feature (deferred)"; cache hits emit no OpRecord so the action list has derived gaps — a cache hit shows as a ghost "served from cache (derived from is_cache/source==ram)" row, never a missing read; STATE_SNAPSHOT/STATE_DELTA are reserved (enum-only) so the State panel header shows a greyed "Δ state events: not yet emitted" chip rather than faking JSON-patch deltas.
dataSourceExploration: The Data Sources panel is a mount tree + per-path file browser — explicitly NOT a per-backend native client, because mirage collapses every backend (S3/Slack/Postgres/Datadog/disk/ram) to one VFS. TOP LEVEL = mounts from getConsoleWorkspace.mounts (_console_mounts_detail over Workspace.mounts()): each row shows prefix (/s3, /database, /slack, /datadog, /scratch), resource type (s3/disk/ram/postgres), mode (read/write/exec) as a small ro/rw chip, and a quiet effect-class dot (scratch/durable-internal/system-of-record/external-effect) with a reversibility tooltip — the most solid per-source metadata we have, reusing mountColor + EffectClassTag. EXPAND a mount = lazy ls via vfsList (server _execute_in_workspace 'ls -la' → _parse_ls_output → {name,type,size}); the tree reuses VFSExplorer's TreeNodeRow vocabulary (chevron, folder/file icon, size, mount-color dot at depth 0). SELECT a file = vfsFile ('cat') in the Console/output dock's "Preview" tab, JSON pretty-printed client-side, with an explicit "preview only · text decode · may be truncated/binary" footer (no binary/truncation handling exists, so we never pretend). PER-TYPE is convention, not custom widgets — and the UI says so: a /database mount renders tables/<t>/{schema.json,data.jsonl,stats.json} as ordinary files, but the file header adds a derived "Table" affordance — if the selected file is schema.json we render columns/types/PK/FK as a small grid and offer a "sample rows" peek of data.jsonl head; Datadog shows logs/<svc>/<date>.jsonl + metrics/*.json as a log/metric tree; Slack as channels/threads/message files. A persistent banner on queryable-looking sources reads "browse-only — live SQL/glob/similarity via query.json + catalog-proxy is designed, not yet callable (NotImplementedError)" so no one mistakes the disk doubles for a query engine. Per-path metadata (fingerprint/revision/modified/consistency) is shown ONLY when real: the file header has a "metadata" line that renders modified/fingerprint/revision when present and otherwise greys them with "not surfaced (ls -la drops these; only S3 SUPPORTS_SNAPSHOT populates ETag/revision)" — honest to the gotcha that _parse_ls_output keeps only name/type/size. THE BIDIRECTIONAL DATA↔TRACE BRIDGE is the panel's headline and the moat tie-in: every file/dir row carries a small "touch count" badge = number of trajectory entries whose mount_prefix==mount and path startsWith(rowPath) (derived client-side from getTrajectory, which already carries path+mount_prefix+kind+effect_class+capture_state). Clicking the badge (or right-click → "Who touched this?") opens a "Touches" list in the Console dock: each read/write with idx, op, bytes, duration_ms, source, effect-class, and the inferred owning step/run (matched by event ordering between TOOL_CALL_START boundaries / timestamp window — labeled INFERRED with the same "≈" marker, because tool_call_id is not stamped on op events yet). Clicking a touch row moves the GLOBAL CURSOR to that idx — so the data tree drives the waterfall and state inspector, completing the bridge. Conversely, when the cursor sits on a VfsOp action, the data tree auto-scrolls to and flashes the touched path (forward direction). Cross-source joins (.relationships) are reserved: a greyed "link to related source" affordance with "RelationshipEntry designed, not implemented." The legacy DataBrowser.tsx (mock /api/tickets REST) is explicitly NOT used here; the panel is VFS-backed only.

Drag-the-playhead time-travel: a bottom scrubber/minimap with a draggable playhead scrubs the workspace through its action history; everything past the cursor dims (future-dimming), and the State inspector animates the overlay growing/shrinking op-by-op — exact for reads/overlay/pending-effects, with backing honestly labeled 'pinned at stand-up'.

Bidirectional data↔trace bridge: every file/dir row carries a touch-count badge; 'Who touched this byte?' lists every read/write (idx·bytes·source·effect-class·INFERRED step) and clicking one jumps the cursor — and conversely landing the cursor on a VfsOp auto-scrolls+flashes that path in the tree.

Skip-action what-if: right-click an action → 'Skip' re-folds state without it under a 'hypothetical' banner (one-click revert), letting a dev prove whether a redundant read or write actually mattered — Redux DevTools skip, grounded in the deterministic trajectory fold.

Command palette (Cmd-K): fuzzy 'go to run-…', 'filter ops on /database', 'jump to last write', 'solo State panel', 'export session bundle', 'reset layout' — keyboard-first navigation befitting a tool you live in.

Solo / dock / tab any panel: double-click a header to maximize one panel full-screen and again to restore; drag panels between dock zones or stack them as tabs; layout presets ('Trace focus', 'Data focus', 'Time-travel') in the Layout menu, with the arrangement persisted per workspace.

Permalink everything: workspace id + cursor idx + selected node encode into the URL so any debugging state — a specific op at a specific action in a specific run — is a shareable link, and 'Export session bundle' hands a fully replayable repro (trajectory + agui trace + manifest) to a teammate via Import.

Honest-by-construction chrome: 'preview only/truncated' on file content, '≈' tie-markers on timestamp-merged actions, greyed fingerprint/revision when ls drops them, ghost 'served from cache (derived)' rows, and greyed 'not yet emitted' rails for lineage/policy/STATE_DELTA — the tool never fabricates data the data plane didn't emit.
leveragesMirageData: Yes, end to end. The Trace waterfall reuses the live Session›Run›Step›ToolCall reducer (aguiEventReducer/replayAguiEvents, RunTracePanel/StepCard/ToolCallRow) and hangs the VfsOp ground-truth leaf (OpRecord: op·path·source·bytes·duration_ms·mount_prefix) beneath each tool call — the data-plane span layer only mirage can produce. The Event Log is the real two-stream merge: relay firehose (useEventStream('/events'), stable global seq; command/op/agent_status/agent_thinking/mock_request/mcp_tool_call/console_*) ⊕ per-session AG-UI events (getSessionTrace; RUN/STEP/THINKING/TEXT/TOOL_CALL/CUSTOM(vfs_op)), merged on timestamp with explicit tie-markers because AG-UI events carry no global seq. The State inspector reconstructs op-by-op from the callable console endpoints — getTrajectory (entries[].idx == ws.ops.records position, the dense cursor), getOverlay (mounts[].changes, change key idx:op:path), getEffects (pending writes minus promoted_keys), getConsoleWorkspace.mounts (_console_mounts_detail: prefix/resource/mode/effect_class) — folding [0..idx] for jump/skip, exactly the deterministic fold replayAguiEvents already proves. The Data Sources panel is the real VFS browser: vfsList ('ls -la' → {name,type,size}) + vfsFile ('cat'), reusing VFSExplorer's tree vocabulary and mountColor/effectClass decorations; the data↔trace bridge is derived from getTrajectory's path+mount_prefix+kind+effect_class+capture_state. Decorations (effect-class, capture-state, derived cache phase via is_cache/source==ram) come from the existing captureState/effectClass libs. Export/Import build on TrajectoryPage.exportJson plus the agui_events trace. Workspace switching/branching uses consoleStore + BranchTree + snapshot/branch/reset. Nothing is invented: where the data plane is silent (catalog-proxy/workspace-vfs NotImplementedError, dropped fingerprint/revision, STATE_SNAPSHOT/DELTA, lineage/policy), the UI renders explicit reserved/greyed/derived states.
risks: The two-stream merge is timestamp-only (AG-UI events have no global seq), so same-ms actions have undefined order and op→step attribution is INFERRED by event ordering/timestamp windows (correlateEvents). Mitigation: '≈' tie-markers + INFERRED labels everywhere, and prioritize the dense trajectory idx for state reconstruction; the real fix is Phase-0 plumbing (stamp tool_call_id/run_id + source/duration_ms/fingerprint/revision on op events, fill vfs_ops.tool_call_id in the coalescer).

Time-travel is only partial: written-mount backing is pinned once at stand-up (one snapshot tar), so byte-exact full-FS state before action N is NOT reconstructable, and cache hits emit no OpRecord (gaps vs real I/O). Mitigation: State panel reconstructs overlay/reads/pending exactly and labels 'Backing: pinned at stand-up'; cache hits render as derived ghost rows; never promise byte-exact full-FS time travel.

Data Sources fidelity is capped by string-parsed ls -la/cat: only name/type/size survive (modified/fingerprint/revision/mode/consistency dropped), and preview has no binary/truncation handling. Mitigation: greyed metadata with honest explanations, 'preview only/truncated' footer, and the SchemaGrid/sample-rows treated as a convention viewer, not a query engine; the persistent 'browse-only — query.json/catalog-proxy not yet callable' banner prevents over-promising.

A dev console watching ALL workspace events can blow past the 2000-event RAM ring and in-memory console caches; the firehose is also GLOBAL not workspace-scoped (only console_* carry workspace_id; op/command use the agent session id). Mitigation: read from arcadia_store-backed paginated/virtualized endpoints, scope client-side by the workspace's session(s), and show a 'not persisted' badge when _setup_persistence degrades to memory (replay/time-travel-after-restart would be empty).

Heavy docked multi-panel UIs risk cognitive overload and performance jank (five live panels + virtualization + cross-highlight on every cursor move). Mitigation: sensible layout presets, collapsible left/bottom docks, solo-on-double-click, debounced cross-filter, and virtualization on the action list/tree; default layout hides the Console drawer until invoked.

Demoting governance (no pending-effects modal, no LIVE red chrome) could let a dev miss that a write would hit a real backend in LIVE mode. Mitigation: keep effect-class/capture-state as quiet but always-present per-write decorations, a non-alarming 'pending N' chip, and a one-line LIVE indicator in the App Bar — enough signal without an ops-product front door.

Compare and Skip-action can be mistaken for real mutations of the run. Mitigation: explicit 'hypothetical' / 'what-if overlay' banners with one-click revert, and Compare clearly framed as a read-only lens over two pinned cursors.

name: Sourcescope — the Bidirectional Data ⇄ Trace Explorer Console
thesis: Because Mirage IS the data plane, the console's front door should be the DATA, not the traces. Sourcescope is a Redux-DevTools-grade debug console scoped to one workspace whose home is a live catalog of mounted sources (S3/disk file trees, Postgres-as-files tables+schema, Slack channels, Datadog logs) — every node decorated with a derived "touched by N traces" badge. The console commits to one inversion the competition structurally cannot copy: navigation flows BOTH ways. From a trace you descend to the exact bytes (trace→data); from any path/table/row you reverse-link to "every step that read or wrote this" (data→trace), joined off the OpRecord ground-truth leaf (mount_prefix+path) that observe.context.record() captures beneath the agent's self-reported tool args. This makes the killer workflow data-correctness debugging: "the agent answered from the WRONG file / a STALE revision" — start at the suspect path, jump to the offending op, scrub the time-travel cursor to see workspace state at that tick. Three modes hang off the data spine: Sources (the home explorer), All Traces (the workspace's run waterfall), and the Action Log + Time-Travel (the Redux centerpiece). The console is honest to the bone: it labels op→step links INFERRED until tool_call_id is stamped, marks cat/ls previews "preview only", dims backing-FS time-travel as "pinned at stand-up", renders cache hits as DERIVED, and reserves greyed panels for lineage/policy/query.json that are schema-designed but NotImplementedError today.
organizingMetaphor: A database/object-store client cross-bred with Redux DevTools — think "DataGrip's schema-tree left rail + DevTools' action timeline", reframed so the schema tree is Mirage's mount catalog and every row has a 'cross-references' (find-usages) gutter that resolves to traces. The single committed metaphor: FIND-USAGES FOR DATA. Just as an IDE answers "who calls this function?", Sourcescope answers "who read/wrote this byte?" — the data-source tree is the symbol index, traces/steps are the call sites, and the time-travel cursor is the debugger's stack-frame scrubber over the workspace world.
informationArchitecture:
WORKSPACE IS THE TOP-LEVEL CONTAINER. A persistent top bar carries (left→right): Sourcescope mark; a Workspace switcher (`<select>` over consoleStore.workspaces, reusing ConsoleLayout's WorkspaceSwitcher); branch + mode as quiet mono decorations (ModeBadge demoted — no red LIVE chrome, no pending-effects counter in chrome per reframe); a global path/run omni-search (⌘K); a connection dot (useEventStream connected) + persisted/in-memory badge. Everything below = 'everything that happened in THIS workspace.'

Three primary MODES as a left vertical rail (icons + labels, keyboard 1/2/3), DATA-FIRST ordering: (1) SOURCES (home, default) — the connected-data catalog; (2) TRACES — all runs/steps waterfall; (3) ACTION LOG — the unified time-travel event stream. A fourth quiet rail item, STATE, opens the reconstructed-world inspector (reuses StatePage's overlay/effective/backing browser). Each mode fills a 3-region body: LEFT NAV (mode-specific tree/list, ~280–340px), CENTER (primary surface), RIGHT INSPECTOR (~380–420px, context-sensitive, collapsible).

THE BRIDGE IS THE CONNECTIVE TISSUE between modes. From SOURCES: clicking a path's 'N traces' gutter opens the right inspector's 'Touched by' list; clicking an entry deep-links to ACTION LOG focused on that op (data→trace). From TRACES: clicking a step's VfsOp leaf opens that path in SOURCES with the op pre-highlighted, or jumps the ACTION LOG cursor to it (trace→data). From ACTION LOG: the cursor selects an action; the right pane shows reconstructed STATE at that tick with diff highlight, and a 'reveal in Sources' / 'open in Traces' pair of deep-links. All three modes therefore share two URL-addressable selections — the current PATH and the current ACTION INDEX (idx into ws.ops.records / seq) — so a permalink like `/ws/{id}/log?cursor=142&path=/database/tables/accounts` restores the exact cross-mode view. Routing extends the existing /console React-Router tree; modes are sibling routes under a workspace-scoped layout. Down/up the data spine (Session›Run›Step›ToolCall›VfsOp) is preserved inside TRACES via the existing RunTracePanel/StepCard/ToolCallRow; the VfsOp leaf is the universal hand-off point to SOURCES and ACTION LOG.
reduxMapping:
ACTION LIST ← the unified workspace stream, assembled CLIENT-SIDE by merging two transports the codebase keeps separate: (a) the global relay firehose (useEventStream('/events'), stable monotonic `seq`) filtered to this workspace's agent session, and (b) per-session AG-UI events (getSessionTrace → replayAguiEvents, per-session `seq`) for RUN/STEP/THINKING/TOOL_CALL/CUSTOM(vfs_op). They are merged on `timestamp`; the UI states honestly that sub-ms ties are timestamp-ordered (a banner: 'unified order is timestamp-merged; a single global seq needs Phase-0 plumbing'). For DATA-PLANE actions specifically, the gap-free `idx` from _console_trajectory (== position in ws.ops.records) is offered as a cleaner secondary cursor and is the one used for state reconstruction. Each row's 'action type' = event `.type` (RUN_STARTED, op, command, agent_thinking, TOOL_CALL_START, vfs_op…); payload = the event dict, pretty-printed in the inspector.

STATE TREE INSPECTOR ← reconstructed workspace state at the cursor, folded from trajectory[0..N]: (i) effective VFS write-overlay per mount (from _console_overlay, change key idx:op:path) rendered as a collapsible tree via the existing OverlayDiff; (ii) mounts list with effect_class (_console_mounts_detail); (iii) reads-so-far set (read ops ≤ N); (iv) pending/captured effects (_console_effects writes not in promoted_keys); (v) the run/step/reasoning/tool sub-tree from the aguiEventReducer snapshot at that timestamp. STATE_SNAPSHOT/STATE_DELTA are shown as a greyed reserved row ('AG-UI state events — enum exists, never emitted').

PER-ACTION DIFF ← diff(stateAt(N-1), stateAt(N)). For a data-plane action this is EXACT and trivial: action N is exactly OpRecord[N], so the diff IS that single op (path, op-kind, +bytes) — already what OverlayDiff renders per change; the changed path glows in both the state tree and the Sources tree. For run-level actions, diff successive reducer snapshots (new thinking delta / new tool call / new step). A small new diff helper is added; inputs already exist.

JUMP-TO / SKIP ← clicking action N moves the cursor and re-folds trajectory[0..N] (jump); SKIP recomputes with idx N omitted ('skip' is labeled a what-if preview, not a re-execution, since we cannot re-drive the agent). replayAguiEvents already proves deterministic fold-from-empty for the run sub-tree.

FUTURE-DIMMING ← every action with index > cursor renders at ~40% opacity with a left 'not-yet-executed' tick; the live tail auto-advances the cursor unless the user has pinned it (Redux 'pause' behavior).

IMPORT / EXPORT ← Export reuses TrajectoryPage.exportJson (dumps ordered entries) plus the agui_events trace; Import loads a saved {trajectory, trace} bundle into a read-only 'replaying saved session' state (cursor scrubs over imported data; live tail disabled).

HONESTY OVERLAY baked into the cursor: a thin legend shows what's reconstructable at N (overlay, reads-so-far, effects, run sub-tree = SOLID) vs NOT (byte-exact backing FS of written mounts = 'pinned at stand-up'; cache-hit reads = DERIVED gaps). When the cursor lands between an expected network read and its absence, a faint 'served from cache (derived)' chip appears instead of a phantom action.

SOURCES is the home mode and the paradigm's whole bet. LEFT NAV is the mount catalog: each entry from _console_mounts_detail shows prefix (e.g. /database, /s3, /slack), resource type (postgres/disk/ram/s3), MountMode (read/write/exec), and a quiet effect-class chip (scratch / durable-internal / system-of-record / external-effect) with a reversibility tooltip — the most solid per-source metadata available. A derived per-mount 'touched by' rollup (count of distinct runs whose ops hit that prefix) sits on the right of each row. CENTER is a per-source browser with a type-aware skin layered over the SAME ls/cat substrate (vfsList/vfsFile, GET /api/sessions/{id}/vfs|vfs/file):

• A reserved, greyed Metadata strip on every file: fingerprint / revision / modified / mode / consistency — shown as '—' with a tooltip explaining _parse_ls_output drops these and they only flow for SUPPORTS_SNAPSHOT backends (S3 ETag); never fabricated.

RIGHT INSPECTOR is THE BRIDGE — 'Touched by' (find-usages for data). For the selected path or table, it lists every OpRecord whose path startswith the selection (derived from _console_trajectory filtered by mount_prefix/path): each row = op kind (read/write/meta) · source · bytes · duration_ms · effect_class · relative time · the inferred run/step label. The killer workflow the inversion unlocks.

Export/Import of the action+trajectory bundle: export the ordered log (reuse exportJson) and the agui trace; import drops the console into a read-only 'replaying saved session' with a scrubbable cursor and disabled live tail.
leveragesMirageData: Every screen is wired to ground-truth Mirage data, not model self-reports. The SOURCES catalog reads mounts/effect-class from _console_mounts_detail (Mount.prefix/.resource.name/.mode + _effect_class_for_mount); the file tree and previews use the real vfsList/vfsFile (GET /api/sessions/{id}/vfs|vfs/file → ls -la/cat → _parse_ls_output), and the table skin parses the actual fixture files (fake_postgres.py: tables/<t>/{schema.json,data.jsonl,stats.json}). The BRIDGE and ACTION LOG derive entirely from ws.ops.records via the shipped _console_trajectory/_console_overlay/_console_effects endpoints — the OpRecord leaf (op·path·source·bytes·duration_ms·mount_prefix·timestamp, kind+effect_class+capture_state) is the join key and the time-travel spine. The TRACES waterfall consumes the AG-UI run stream through the existing aguiEventReducer/sessionRunStore (RUN/STEP/THINKING/TOOL_CALL/CUSTOM(vfs_op)) and reuses RunTracePanel/StepCard/ToolCallRow/ReasoningBlock; the unified action list merges that with the relay firehose (useEventStream + stream_events seq). STATE reuses StatePage's overlay/effective/backing browser and BranchTree over Workspace.snapshot/branch/reset. Decorations (effect_class, capture_state, reversibility, mount color) come from the real _console_* derivations and existing CaptureBadge/EffectClassTag/OverlayDiff/LiveWorldPanel/mountColor utilities. The unique-leverage payoff is explicit: because these ops are observed at observe.context.record() BELOW the tool args, Touched-by and the wrong-file/stale-revision workflow surface bytes the agent actually touched — a correctness signal no wrapper-based competitor (LangSmith/Langfuse/Phoenix) can produce.
risks: Two-counter merge is the central technical bet and it's lossy: AG-UI events carry only a per-session seq and never pass through _persist_and_broadcast, so the unified Action Log orders by timestamp and same-ms events have undefined order. The honesty banner mitigates UX but a truly correct single cursor needs Phase-0 (route AG-UI through _persist_and_broadcast, stamp run_id/step_id/tool_call_id on relay op events).

op→step attribution is INFERRED by event ordering / timestamp windows (correlateEventsToSteps), not joined — Touched-by run/step labels can mis-bucket on overlapping or zero-duration steps. Until tool_call_id is stamped on vfs_op emission, the bridge's data→step precision is best-effort and must stay labeled.

The demo makes exotic sources look richer than they are: /database, /s3, /slack, /datadog are all Fake*Resource(DiskResource) dirs, so the table/channel/log skins are conventions over cat/ls with NO live query, NO live ETag/revision, NO real backend. If the 'derived from files' and 'preview only' honesty chips are softened, the console will over-promise (catalog-proxy + query.json are 100% NotImplementedError).

fingerprint/revision/modified/mode/consistency are dropped by _parse_ls_output and only flow for SUPPORTS_SNAPSHOT backends (S3 ETag) — so the metadata strip and any drift/version UI are mostly '—' on demo data. Risk of designing affordances (drift badges, revision pickers) that can't be populated without surfacing FileStat via a structured FS read.

Time-travel is only partial: VFS overlay/reads-so-far/effects/run-sub-tree re-fold exactly, but byte-exact backing FS of written mounts is pinned once at stand-up and cache hits emit no OpRecord — the action stream has real gaps vs true I/O. Backing time-travel and 'skip-action re-execution' must stay framed as what-if/deferred, never byte-exact.

Scale: a workspace-scoped console watching ALL events cannot ride the 2000-event RAM ring, the 5000-deque firehose, or the in-memory console caches — Action Log and Touched-by must paginate/virtualize off arcadia_store, and derived runs/steps/tool_calls/vfs_ops are currently WRITE-ONLY (no read method) so historical (post-restart) views need new queries or a re-stand-up.

Workspace scoping is leaky: useEventStream('/events') is GLOBAL and only console_* events carry workspace_id; relay op/command events key by the agent SESSION id, not the console workspace id. Correctly filtering 'everything in THIS workspace' requires mapping workspace→session and client-side filtering, and persistence can silently degrade to in-memory (empty trace/time-travel after restart) — the UI must distinguish 'clean' from 'not persisted'.

Data-first IA is a real bet against habit: engineers may expect a trace-first console (LangSmith muscle memory). Sources-as-home only pays off if Touched-by and the wrong-file workflow are immediately discoverable; otherwise the inversion reads as an extra hop to the traces they wanted.
